body.statement: For either independent exact-count assignment with known hit probabilities \(r_C\to r\in\Delta_K(\rho)\) or independent nominal-label Bernoulli assignment with \(r_C\to r=Bp\), the total calibrated Horvitz--Thompson estimator satisfies \(\mathbb E(\widehat U_C)=U_C\) for every \(C\), and the set of all subsequential asymptotic covariance matrices of \(\sqrt C(\widehat U_C-U_C)\) over arrays in \(\mathcal P(f,\mu_0)\) is exactly \(\mathfrak S(r;f,\mu_0)\). Every \(\lambda\in\Lambda(f,\mu_0)\) is attained by a deterministic sequence of unrestricted binary schedules, and no compatible sequence has a covariance outside this image. Moreover, for every rational \(Dtest\), both support values of \(\operatorname{tr}(Dtest\,\Omega)\) over this image are finite linear-program optima over \(\Lambda(f,\mu_0)\), with rational primal and dual certificates when \(f\) and \(r\) are rational.
body.justification: This replaces the false point covariance by the complete randomization-compatible covariance set while keeping the finite-sample estimator defined on every randomization outcome.
body.gap: AronowGreenLee2014 treats a two-potential-outcome scalar variance, GaoGeQian2025 treats generic multi-marginal functionals, and HarshawMiddletonSavje2026 optimizes conservative quadratic upper bounds; none derives the full exact-slice covariance image as the input to allocation choice.
body.consumer: A saturation trial can certify every covariance matrix that its policy-selection analysis must protect against without adding a cross-policy coupling model.
